title: Box Read Across Pages (Print Only)

illustrates.quote: When a single box is shown across print pages and it is read as if it were on a single page, and there is no other text on either page, transcribe it as a single box. Use combined page numbers, e.g., 22-23, a22-23, etc. Box lines may be omitted if the content will fit on a single braille page without them. Option: Tables printed across facing print pages may be produced as facing braille pages, if all the material will fit on the two pages. (See Formats, §11.13, Wide Tables: Facing Pages.)

blocks.text: An open-book illustration: a table of verb tenses ('Indicative') split across facing print pages 22 (left) and 23 (right), joined by a curved arrow above the gutter pointing left-to-right to show the table is meant to be read as one continuous whole.
blocks.features: Black silhouette open-book graphic with rounded page edges and a curved directional arrow above the spine; a schematic diagram illustrating the concept of a table spanning facing pages, not a literal textbook page excerpt.

14-row x 6-column verb-conjugation table ('Indicative' mood): the tense-name column plus the 'I'/'you' columns fall on the left (page 22) half; 'he, she, it'/'we'/second 'you' columns fall on the right (page 23) half. Page numbers '22'/'23' are printed at the top corners of the respective halves. Confirmed directly against a 250dpi crop of the PDF page image (p.189, footer 7-5): the 'Indicative' header cell is shaded light purple/lavender; the remaining header cells on the right half are plain white.

print.notes: Print-only illustrative figure captioned 'Example 7-3: Box Read Across Pages (Print Only)'. No braille transcription is given anywhere in the source for this example -- it exists solely to show print readers/transcribers the print layout situation that rule 7.4.1.a addresses (a single box/table split across facing pages with no other text on either page).
print.surroundingText: Immediately follows rule 7.4.1.a in the running text (see illustrates.quote); the rule's own text is what this figure depicts.
print.printFeatures: Full-width black-and-white open-book silhouette graphic with a curved directional arrow at the top; page numbers 22/23 printed inside the book corners; the table itself uses light shading to distinguish its header row.

braille.notes: No braille given in the source -- the example is explicitly captioned '(Print Only)' and no braille transcription follows the caption anywhere in the extracted text (confirmed: nothing but four blank lines, 5499-5502, sit between the caption at line 5498 and the next content, rule 7.4.1.b at line 5503).

resolution: Content agreed identically between the two runs (table headers/rows byte-identical; both independently confirm print-only, no braille anywhere in the source). Corrected the header-cell shading colour: A recorded it as 'light-blue-tinted', B as 'light purple/lavender' -- confirmed directly against a 250dpi crop of the PDF page image (references/bana/braille-formats-2016.pdf, p.189) that the 'Indicative' cell is light purple/lavender, not blue; B's reading used.
